name: TRAPPIST-1
tagline: Seven Earth-size worlds around a star barely bigger than Jupiter.
history: TRAPPIST-1 is an ultracool dwarf only slightly larger than Jupiter, yet seven rocky planets transit it — the largest batch of Earth-size worlds found around a single star. All seven orbit closer than Mercury orbits the Sun, packed so tightly that from one surface the neighbors would appear Moon-sized in the sky. Planets e, f and g sit in the temperate zone where liquid water could persist, though tidal locking may leave each with a permanent day and night side. JWST is now probing their atmospheres for the first constraints on habitability around red dwarfs — the most common stars in the galaxy.
source: NASA Exoplanet Archive; Nature (Gillon et al., 2017)
